statement.text:
Let Γ be an infinite directed graph, and Γ the underlying undirected graph.
Suppose that the graph Γ admits a vertex-transitive group of automorphisms, and
the graph Γ is connected and of finite valency. Does there exist a positive integer
k (possibly depending on Γ) such that for any positive integer n there is a directed
path of length at most k · n in the graph Γ whose initial and terminal vertices are at
distance at least n in the graph Γ?
    Comment of 2005: It is proved that there exists a positive integer k ′ (depending
only on the valency of Γ) such that for any positive integer n there is a directed path
of length at most k ′ · n2 in the graph Γ whose initial and terminal vertices are at
distance at least n in the graph Γ (V. I. Trofimov, Europ. J. Combinatorics, 27, no. 5
(2006), 690–700).                                                         V. I. Trofimov
